claim: Schueth restates the constant-curvature-consistent b_1(C) formula for an orbifold cone point of order n, b_1(C) = [(1/360)(n^3-1/n)+(1/36)(n-1/n)] K(p), with explicit attribution to Dryden-Gordon-Greenwald-Webb (Michigan J. Math. 56 (2008) 205-238).
stance_target: The manuscript's claim that arXiv:2511.22255 restates the constant-curvature b_1 cone formula with attribution to DGGW
scope_conditions: Two-dimensional Riemannian orbifold cone point of order n; formula depends only on local Gauss curvature K(p), hence applies unchanged to constant curvature
quoted_support: For cone points C of order n in two-dimensional Riemannian orbifolds, it was shown in [Dryden et al.] that b_1(C)=(1/360(n^3-1/n)+1/36(n-1/n))K(p), where K is the Gauss curvature and p the point corresponding to C in an orbifold chart.

claim: Schueth's new curved-conic-singularity invariant b_{1/2}(C) is nonzero only when f''(0) != 0, which is proved equivalent to the Gaussian curvature blowing up at the tip (|K(p)| -> infinity as p -> C); the paper further establishes that f''(0)=0 identically for ANY orbifold cone point (constant curvature or not), so orbifold cone points never exhibit curvature blow-up at the tip and the new invariant vanishes there.
stance_target: The manuscript's claim that Schueth's curved-cone results do not apply to constant-curvature orbifold cones because there is no curvature blow-up at the tip
scope_conditions: Rotationally-symmetric conic singularity g=dr^2+f(r)^2 dtheta^2 vs. orbifold cone points of any (including constant) curvature
quoted_support: Since K=-f''/f in the coordinates from (1), the inequality f''(0)!=0 is equivalent to |K(p)|->infinity for p->C... If f''(0)!=0 in (1), then, unlike in the orbifold case, half powers of t can occur in the middle sum of (2), and logarithmic terms can occur, too. [...] Passing to an orbifold cone point of order n just corresponds to passing from f to f/n, so f''(0)=0 still holds for cone points in orbisurfaces.

claim: The general (not-necessarily-constant-curvature) orbifold b_2(C) formula was already published by Schueth in an earlier 2019 paper (arXiv:1812.06119 = Ann. Inst. Fourier 69 (2019) no.7 2827-2855), as a linear combination of K(p)^2 and (Delta K)(p); Ucar's arXiv:1711.03405 gives all b_l(C) for constant curvature as b_l(C)=kappa^l (1/n) p_l(n) with deg p_l = 2l+2.
stance_target: Whether higher constant-curvature cone coefficients b_2/b_3 require new computation for the manuscript's planned extension
scope_conditions: Two-dimensional Riemannian orbifolds, cone point of order n; general curvature for b_2, constant curvature kappa for all b_l via Ucar
quoted_support: In [Schueth 2019], the author obtained a similar formula for b_2(C) in the same context; b_2(C) turns out to be a linear combination of K(p)^2 and (Delta K)(p), where the coefficients are, again, rational functions of the order of the cone point. [...] Ucar obtained explicit formulas for all b_l(C) for cone points C of two-dimensional orbifolds under the special assumption that the orbifold has constant curvature kappa in R. [...] b_l(C) can then be written as kappa^l times (1/n) p_l(n), where p_l is a certain polynomial of order 2l+2.
